provenance.author: this repository
provenance.method: exhaustion over all triples of 4-qubit stabilizer states, via a pivot and two quotients

notes: Upgraded from reproduced to verified (exact: true, we* + @mizopl, 2026-11-10, 0.5 s) via verify_challenge/cert_qubit_galois_m3_m4.py: scaling |H>^4 by cos(pi/8)^(-4) gives (|0> + (sqrt(2) - 1)|1>)^4 = A_4 + sqrt(2) B_4 in Z[i]^16 + sqrt(2) Z[i]^16; by Galois descent over Q(i, sqrt(2)) / Q(i), any rank-3 decomposition must contain P_4 = span_{Q(i)}(A_4, B_4) and project to a single 1D ray in Q(i)^16 / P_4, whereas exact primitive Z[i]-ray canonicalisation across all 36,720 4-qubit stabilizer states finds 0 states in P_4 and maximum ray group size 2 (< 3). Prior reproduced record (verify_challenge/cert_qubit_h_m4_rank3.py): Settles chi(|H>^4) = 4 with the verified rank-4 decomposition, both directions machine-checked, and reproduces the value of Bravyi, Smith, and Smolin from scratch. Every rank-3 triple over the 36720 four-qubit stabilizer states is excluded: 8.69 million collinear-in-quotient candidates arise and every one is three states of a single two-dimensional stabilizer subspace, whose span cannot contain the target once rank 2 is excluded in the same pass; no independent collinear triple exists at all. The exclusion is numerical and rests on a margin: the closest any two key-adjacent non-parallel quotient directions come to parallel is 0.9877 against a threshold of 1 - 1e-6, and the certificate refuses to print its claim if that clearance falls under 0.01. The H-type state at m=3, whose rank-3 decomposition is verified on the board, is the positive control.
